question.text: Per NISM Ch 2.6.1 citing SEBI circulars from 2017, Indian Category III AIFs are permitted to invest in commodity derivatives up to what proportion of investable funds in ONE underlying commodity?

answer.text: 50% of investable funds in one underlying commodity.
25% of investable funds in one underlying commodity.
10% of investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to SEBI reporting requirements.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 2.6.1, 'Indian Category III AIFs are permitted by SEBI to invest in all commodity derivatives products that are being traded on the commodity derivatives exchanges. They can invest up to 10 percent of the investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to the reporting requirements set forth by SEBI' — reference SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CDMRD/DMP/CIR/P/2017/61 dated June 21, 2017. **The Trap:** Option A is false — concentration limits exist. Options B and C are common distractor percentages used on NISM exams; candidates who don't recall the exact 10% figure drift here. **Cross-Exam Context:** VIII (Equity Derivatives) tests derivative market mechanics but not this AIF-specific limit. XIX-B tests it from sales. XIX-C manager exam tests the operational limit. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build the 10% per-commodity cap into your fund's pre-trade compliance check, with a soft limit at 8% to accommodate mark-to-market drift. Hitting 10.01% on a month-end is a reportable breach that invites SEBI scrutiny.
